curriculum.title: Second Temple Context without a New Authority

core.big_idea: Intertestamental evidence helps explain Jesus' world without becoming an independent source of Christian doctrine.

core.metanarrative_position: Second Temple context: noncanonical evidence illuminates language and history while Scripture remains doctrinal authority.

claims.statement: Daniel 7 describes one like a son of man receiving dominion and an everlasting kingdom.

claims.statement: Second Temple Jewish writings can illuminate concepts, language, and historical expectations in the New Testament world.

claims.interpretive_hinge: The distinction between historical or contextual usefulness and canonical doctrinal authority.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify genre and context, separate direct observation from synthesis or inference, and connect the passage to the whole-Bible story without forced symbolism.

learning.foundation_objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that intertestamental evidence helps explain Jesus' world without becoming an independent source of Christian doctrine.
learning.extension_objective: Locate the lesson in the whole-Bible story and distinguish direct textual claims from later synthesis or application.
know: The central passage is Daniel 7:13-14; selected Septuagint and historical context.

understand: Biblical meaning depends on context and genre.
Application should follow what the text supports rather than replace it.
practise: Use one observation question before giving an interpretation.
Choose one historical fact about the New Testament world and discuss how it clarifies a passage without becoming doctrine.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, and love.
success_evidence: Student can retell or summarize the central passage.
Student can state the big idea without adding unsupported details.

zero_prep_card.objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that intertestamental evidence helps explain Jesus' world without becoming an independent source of Christian doctrine.
zero_prep_card.read: Daniel 7:13-14; selected Septuagint and historical context
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask: What do you notice first in this passage, before we explain what it means?
say: Daniel 7 describes one like a son of man receiving dominion and an everlasting kingdom.
The Septuagint is an ancient Greek translation tradition of Jewish Scriptures important for textual and linguistic study.
Intertestamental evidence helps explain Jesus' world without becoming an independent source of Christian doctrine.
We will separate what the passage says from what we infer or apply.
ask: What happens or is said in the passage?

preparation.passage_context: Second Temple context: noncanonical evidence illuminates language and history while Scripture remains doctrinal authority.
text_observations: Daniel 7 describes one like a son of man receiving dominion and an everlasting kingdom.
The Septuagint is an ancient Greek translation tradition of Jewish Scriptures important for textual and linguistic study.
Second Temple Jewish writings can illuminate concepts, language, and historical expectations in the New Testament world.
Within this curriculum, noncanonical ancient sources may inform context but do not independently establish Christian doctrine.
interpretation_notes: Start with the principal passage before moving to supporting texts.
Keep genre and original audience visible.
Label synthesis, historical context, and application rather than presenting them as quotations.
theological_guardrails: All claims about dating, authorship, textual families, and specific Second Temple movements require source verification before publication.
Do not imply the Septuagint was one uniform bound book identical in every community.
Do not dismiss ancient noncanonical sources as useless simply because they are not the operative canon.

likely_questions.question: Why does Jude quote material also found outside the Protestant canon?
likely_questions.purpose: A canonical author can cite or echo a known source without thereby declaring the entire source canonical.

likely_questions.question: Why study the Septuagint?
likely_questions.purpose: It helps with Greek wording, textual history, and the Bible used in many ancient Jewish and Christian contexts.

accessibility.plain_language_rule: Prefer short sentences, define unfamiliar biblical terms, and do not require independent reading beyond the segment.
neurodiversity_supports: Give instructions one step at a time.
Allow verbal, written, or pointing responses.
Preview transitions and allow a pass option.
sensory_notes: No activity requires loud sound, forced touch, or competitive speed.
non_reader_support: Teacher or parent may read aloud.
Use sequence cards, symbols, or oral responses.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of private family circumstances.
Do not require public confession or religious decision.
Do not use physical touch without consent.
safeguarding.teacher_response: If a child discloses harm, danger, abuse, severe distress, or unmet basic needs, follow the congregation safeguarding process rather than trying to investigate in class.
